To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the frequency and prognosic impact of recurrent ST-segment elevations in patients with acute ST-elevation myocardial infarctions treated with intravenous streptokinase was investigated.

In patients treated with thrombolytic agents, recurrences of ECG signs of myocardial ischemia are frequent during the first 24 hours after initiation of thrombolysis and are associated with a higher rate of subsequent in-hospital re-infarction and long-term vessel occlusion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the early detection of myocardial infarcts, which are often missed because of their atypical symptoms, especially when the patients are not aware of the infarction and do not present with chest pain.
the frequency and prognosic impact of early recurrence of the ST‐segment elevation after initial ST‐segment resolution in patients with an acute myocardial infarcion (MI).
the development of a new method for the determination of the infarction-related ST-segment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarctions who have early reperfusion during intravenous thrombolytic treatment are at increased risk of subsequent reinfarctions if they have recurrent ST-segment elevations during the first 24 hours.

early recurrent ST‐segment elevation, occurring during the first 24 hours after initiation of thrombolysis, is a marker of a higher risk for in‐hospital re‐infarction and for long‐term occlusion of the reperfused infraction related vessel in patients with ST‐segment elevation myocardial infarctions.

the early recurrence of ST‐elevation in patients with an initially reperfusing infarct artery indicates that the vessel is not stably open, and is associated with a higher risk of subsequent reinfarction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

patients with ST-segment resolution after reperfusion have a high risk of early recurrent ST-elevation and subsequent in-hospital re-infarction, which is associated with a high rate of occluded arteries during follow-up.

the presence of recurrent ST-segment changes in patients with acute infarction who have had an early ST-segment resolution after thrombolysis indicates a higher risk for reinfarction, and a higher rate of infarct-related vessel occlusion at follow-up.

the recurrence of ST-segment elevations during the first 24 hours after the initiation of thrombolysis is associated with an increased risk of reinfaction during hospitalization and with a long-term occlusion rate of the infarction-related artery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
early recurrent ST‐segment elevation after thrombolysis is common, and is associated with increased risk of recurrent myocardial infarctions, and with a high risk of infarct-related vessel patency.
the ST-segment resolution is not a reliable marker for the reperfusion of the infarction-related artery.
the presence of recurrent ST elevation in the first 24 hours after thrombolysis is associated with higher risk of re-infarction and long-term occlusion.
